narrative.overview: The portfolio behaves like a quiet gallery assembled by an engineer: the shell is disciplined, high-contrast, and deliberately recessive, while project evidence occupies the visual foreground. Generous empty space, a strict sans-serif hierarchy, and square-edged surfaces create technical credibility without imitating a dashboard. Amber is used sparingly as a curatorial mark—showing selection, focus, and action rather than decorating the page. Personality is concentrated in Miguel's portrait, expanding wordmark, rotatable cat, alternating project layouts, drawer transition, and dry copy.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome light and dark worlds with one scarce amber signal.
Editorial-scale type, long vertical rhythm, and intentional negative space.
Flat, square-edged structure; rounding is reserved for functional or physical forms.
Project media and case-study content lead; chrome remains quiet.
Small moments of personality rather than continuous visual spectacle.
Equivalent desktop, mobile, keyboard, and reduced-motion experiences.

rules.name: The Amber Annotation Rule
rules.body: Amber marks attention, selection, or movement. If an element is neither interactive nor meaningfully selected, it normally should not be amber.

rules.name: The Neutral Canvas Rule
rules.body: Large surfaces remain paper or ink. Do not introduce colored page panels to make an empty area feel busier; the negative space is structural.

rules.name: The Artwork Containment Rule
rules.body: The rose/teal/amber generated palette stays inside project-card loading and image-error states.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Barlow is the voice of the interface. Add another family only for a genuine content requirement, never to manufacture variety.

rules.name: The Weight Is Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Light body copy and strong headings create the signature contrast; avoid collapsing everything to regular or semibold.

rules.name: The Case Study Is Reading Rule
rules.body: Markdown headings are deliberately smaller, mixed case, and more closely spaced than landing-page headings because the user has entered a reading surface.

rules.name: The Long Page Rule
rules.body: Each home section gets enough vertical room to read as a chapter; do not pack profile, work, and social into a dashboard grid.

rules.name: The Same Story Rule
rules.body: Drawer and canonical project surfaces share content structure and component behavior rather than drifting into separate designs.

rules.name: The Mobile Reflow Rule
rules.body: Reorder into a clear reading sequence; do not horizontally squeeze the desktop composition or introduce page-level horizontal scrolling.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Shadows indicate a floating or transient layer. Static content and ordinary cards stay flat.

rules.name: The Legible Glass Rule
rules.body: Transparency is never allowed to make foreground and background copy compete. Increase surface opacity before increasing blur.

rules.name: The Structural Backdrop Rule
rules.body: The drawer backdrop explains modality and blocks background interaction; it is not decorative haze.

rules.name: The Radius Has Meaning Rule
rules.body: Do not round a surface merely to make it feel modern. Use rounding for physical forms, compact controls, clipped media, or the bottom-sheet metaphor.

rules.name: The Border Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: Prefer a neutral hairline or tonal shift when a flat surface needs separation.

dos: Do let projects, portrait, and the cat provide visual interest while interface chrome stays monochrome and quiet.
Do use semantic theme variables and verify light, dark, and system appearances.
Do reserve amber for focus, selection, links, and meaningful interaction feedback.
Do preserve the generous vertical rhythm and 970px home reading width.
Do keep project cards flat, media-led, and alternating on desktop.
Do use the established spacing scale and recurring 750px responsive breakpoint.
Do keep body copy readable, light in weight, and constrained to useful line lengths.
Do maintain 44px targets for primary compact controls and visible keyboard focus everywhere.
Do provide reduced-motion behavior for continuous or decorative animation.
Do treat the drawer and canonical project page as two presentations of the same story.
Do verify floating glass over real text in both themes; opacity protects readability.
Do update this document and `.impeccable/design.json` when durable visual tokens or patterns change.
donts: Don't add gradients, background lines, blobs, or color fields to page chrome merely to fill negative space.
Don't turn sections, project cards, errors, or privacy content into generic rounded cards.
Don't introduce pills, badge clouds, glass on every surface, or large soft shadows.
Don't use amber as a large background or a second body-text color; its scarcity is the point.
Don't introduce another font family or replace Barlow without an explicit identity decision.
Don't make Markdown headings compete with the project title or landing-page headline.
Don't hide critical behavior behind hover or remove the global focus treatment.
Don't squeeze the alternating desktop grid onto mobile; reflow it to one reading column.
Don't animate without purpose or ignore `prefers-reduced-motion` for continuous effects.
Don't replace the portrait, cat, drawer, monochrome/amber language, or authored personality with a generic portfolio template.
